queries.text: Schopenhauer, “On Women” (Parerga and Paralipomena), translated from the author’s Portuguese; the public-domain English version is T. Bailey Saunders’s. “Presas” and “colmilhos” both mean tusks in English, hence the repetition (“elephants with tusks, wild boars with tusks”); the German has Stoßzähne/Hauer.
The original has “phalus erectus”; spelling corrected to “phallus erectus” (pseudo-Latin, kept as in the original).
Lévi, Dogma and Ritual of High Magic, translated from the author’s Portuguese; compare Waite’s public-domain “Transcendental Magic” (1896).
